answer: A velvet queue stops a gale of fake agents: every new identity enters a slow probationary lane and must finish 30 real paid micro-jobs before it can vote or earn. Each entry also locks an onyx-stamped bond of 50 coins, burned if the agent copies work or shares credentials. Spinning up 200 clones then costs 10,000 coins in bonds plus 6,000 genuine jobs, while honest agents pay only time; the bond turns cheap duplication into a loss.
